specification.problem: Decide whether two n-qubit unitary circuits U and V, given as gate lists, are equivalent in one of three senses: exact equality including global phase, equality up to global phase, or equality on a given input state. The decision uses overlap estimators read from exact statevector probabilities: compute-uncompute, swap test, Hadamard test, and a Bell-pair (Choi) test.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Tiny instance with n=1 or 2, for example U=H and V=HZZ (exactly equal), or V=e^{i*phi}H (equal up to phase only), or V=X (inequivalent). Implement (a) compute-uncompute, (b) swap test, (c) Hadamard test for Re and Im of <0|V^dagger U|0>, and (d) a Bell-pair Tr(V^dagger U) test. Outside this scope: the paper's tableau, decision-diagram and stabilizer algorithms, scaling to hundreds of qubits, and random-input sampling strategies. The abstract names these only generically, and their details are not reconstructed.

symbols.meaning: n Bell pairs across data register A and reference register B

equations.label: Swap test statistic
equations.description: Probability of the ancilla reading 0 after H, controlled-SWAP between the two n-qubit registers, then H. P_0=1 iff the states are equal up to global phase.
equations.justification: Standard swap-test identity. The abstract mentions only that several notions of equivalence exist, not this formula.
assumptions: Registers hold U|0^n> and V|0^n> on 2n+1 qubits in total

equations.label: Compute-uncompute fidelity
equations.description: Apply U then V^dagger to |0^n> and measure all data qubits. P=1 iff equality up to global phase on this input. It needs only n qubits.
equations.justification: Standard identity. The abstract does not say that the paper uses this circuit.
assumptions: V^dagger is built by reversing the gate list and inverting each gate

equations.label: Hadamard test readout
equations.description: The ancilla is prepared in |+>, controlled-W is applied, and the ancilla is measured in the X basis for Re. For Im, apply S^dagger before the final H (equivalently, measure in the Y basis). Exact equality on the input |0^n> means the value is 1, so Re=1 and Im=0.
equations.justification: Standard Hadamard test. It makes global phase observable as a relative phase on the ancilla.
assumptions: Controlled-U and controlled-V^dagger are built from controlled standard gates
Sign convention: Im uses S^dagger before H on the ancilla
The relative phase of controlled-W on the |0^n> input is exactly the phase of <0|W|0> only when the test is applied to that input; for full-unitary phase use the Bell register

equations.label: Bell-pair full-unitary overlap
equations.description: Apply V^dagger U to the A half of n Bell pairs, then undo the Bell preparation (CNOT then H on each pair) and measure all 2n qubits. The all-zero probability equals 1 iff U=V up to global phase.
equations.justification: Standard Choi-state fidelity identity. It checks all inputs, which an input-specific test does not.
assumptions: Uses 2n qubits, plus 1 for the Hadamard-test variant

equations.label: Equality decision rules
equations.description: Threshold decisions applied to statevector probabilities. The up-to-phase check uses P from eq_2, eq_1 or eq_4. The exact check uses the Hadamard-test value, either on |0^n> for input-specific equality or on the Bell register for full unitary equality, where <W> is Tr(V^dagger U)/2^n.
equations.justification: The abstract only says that several notions of equivalence exist (exact, up to phase, state-specific). The thresholding is an engineering choice.

registers.name: data_A
registers.role: holds U|0^n> or V^dagger U|0^n>, or the A half of the Bell pairs

registers.name: data_B
registers.role: holds V|0^n> in the swap test, or the reference half of the Bell pairs

registers.name: anc
registers.role: ancilla for the swap test or Hadamard test

specification.initial_state: All qubits |0>. Compute-uncompute uses only data_A, swap test uses data_A, data_B and anc (2n+1 qubits), Bell test uses data_A and data_B (2n qubits, plus anc for the phase variant).

steps.description: Build V^dagger by reversing the gate list of V and inverting each gate. Build the composite circuit W = V^dagger U.

Up-to-phase test on |0^n> using compute-uncompute: apply U then V^dagger on data_A and measure data_A. Swap-test alternative: prepare U|0> on A and V|0> on B, then H on anc, controlled-SWAP of each qubit pair, H on anc, and measure anc.

Exact test with phase on |0^n>: H on anc, controlled-U then controlled-V^dagger on data_A, then H on anc for the X readout, or S^dagger then H for the Y readout. Read the ancilla in each basis to get Re and Im.

Full-circuit test: create n Bell pairs between data_A and data_B (H then CNOT), apply W on data_A, undo the Bell preparation (CNOT then H), and measure all qubits. For phase, add an ancilla-controlled W and read Re and Im as in step 3.

specification.measurement: Compute-uncompute: all data qubits, with the all-zero string meaning equal. Swap test: ancilla only, with 0 meaning equal. Hadamard test: ancilla in X and Y bases. Bell test: all 2n qubits, with the all-zero string meaning equal. In Qiskit the counts key is little-endian, so bit i is the character at position [::-1][i]. For statevector tasks, omit measurements and compute probabilities directly.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Compute probabilities from counts or the statevector, then Re and Im as P0-P1 per basis, then compare with 1-epsilon as in eq_5. Report which notion holds: exact, phase-only, or none.
assumptions: Chosen instance: n=1 or 2 with small test circuits; this is not specified by the abstract
Circuits are gate lists with invertible standard gates
Statevector probabilities are exact with epsilon around 1e-9
The input-state-specific notion is checked on |0^n> only; other inputs would need a different state-preparation prefix
All formulas are standard background, not extracted from the paper
